original_question: Are there transcendental entire functions f such that every Liouville number x is sent to another Liouville number f(x)?
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Question 3.27 (Mahler): the existence of an entire transcendental function that maps Liouville numbers to Liouville numbers.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target almost verbatim: it asks for existence, it uses the correct class of functions (transcendental entire functions), it quantifies over all Liouville-number inputs, and it asks that the Liouville property be preserved under f.
missing_details: The exact item in the paper is an open question, namely Question 3.27 (Mahler) in Section 3.4.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say that f is an entire function of one complex variable, i.e. f: C -> C.
To make the statement self-contained, one should define a Liouville number explicitly: a real number xi such that for every n >= 1 there exist integers p and q >= 2 with 0 < |xi - p/q| < q^(-n).
The quantified inputs x are real numbers, since Liouville numbers are real in this context.
The paper does not require f(x) to be different from x; it only requires f(x) itself to be a Liouville number.
Question 3.27 imposes no extra assumptions on coefficients, growth, order, or arithmetic nature of f, so none of these should be added.
If one wants complete terminological clarity, 'transcendental entire' should be understood in the standard sense: entire and not a polynomial.
refined_question: Let L be the set of Liouville numbers, i.e. the real numbers xi such that for every n >= 1 there exist integers p and q >= 2 with 0 < |xi - p/q| < q^(-n). Does there exist a transcendental entire function f: C -> C such that f(L) is contained in L?
justification: The draft is essentially the same as the paper's official formulation: Waldschmidt states in Section 3.4, Question 3.27, 'Are there entire transcendental functions f(z) such that if x is a Liouville number then so is f(x)?' The surrounding paragraph places it among open problems on the arithmetic study of values of power series and does not add any further hypotheses on f. Therefore the sharp paper-faithful rewrite should keep exactly this existence question and should only add the standard definition of Liouville number, the ambient domain f: C -> C, and the implicit fact that x is a real input.
